newsitem.title: UK: UK petrol price drop hints at competition anew - DTI.
newsitem.headline: UK petrol price drop hints at competition anew - DTI.

text.p: A drop in U.K. petrol prices at the start of this year reflects a possible "resumption of price led competition" in the competitive domestic retail market, the Department of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday.

The price of four-star petrol, super unleaded and premium unleaded fell by 0.8, 0.3 and 0.1 pence per litre, respectively, between mid-December and mid-January, the DTI said in its latest statistical report on energy output and consumption.
"These falls are a result of lower crude oil prices and are also possibly a reflection of a resumption of price led competition," DTI said.
The three-month average, however, for November 1996 to January 1997 was sharply higher than the year ago period, it said.
The average for four-star was 7.7 pct higher than the previous year period, super unleaded 15.2 pct higher and premium unleaded 11.1 pct higher, it said.
